title.rendered: Let’s Go, Let’s Go, Let’s Go

content.rendered:
Hank Ballard was one of the founding fathers of rock and roll, releasing several hit songs in the early fifties and writing one of rock’s breakthrough hits, “The Twist” (made famous by Chubby Checker).

Bruce considered him an influence and an inspiration, and after Ballard passed away in early March 2003, Bruce paid tribute by covering Ballard’s greatest hit, “Let’s Go, Let’s Go, Let’s Go,” twice that week.

For the second performance in Richmond, Bruce brought two friends on stage to help him pay homage: Bruce Hornsby, and old Steel Mill bandmate Robbin Thompson. Here’s that performance:

“Let’s Go, Let’s Go, Let’s Go” peaked at number 6 on the charts. It was Ballard’s last and greatest hit.

Let’s Go, Let’s Go, Let’s Go
First performed: March 4, 2003 (Jacksonville, FL)
Last performed: March 6, 2003 (Richmond, VA)

© September 26, 2018

excerpt.rendered: Days after Hank Ballard’s passing, Bruces Springsteen and Hornsby (along with former Steel Mill bandmate Robbin Thompson) pay tribute by playing Ballard’s last great hit.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Twist
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: It's the biggest rock and roll single in history, but Bruce only ever covered it once.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Train Ride
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bruce wasn't Steel Mill's only songwriter. Co-lead vocalist Robbin Thompson contributed his own song to the band's set lists, but their version was a far cry from Mercy Flight's original.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dancing in the Street
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bruce Springsteen has given us hundreds of fantastic covers over the years. This isn't one of them. (But it's worth a listen anyway.)

jetpack-related-posts.title: Roll of the Dice: Goin’ Back to Georgia
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When Bruce walked into a recording studio for only the second time, he recorded one of his earliest crowd-pleasers with his band, Steel Mill. Listen to that studio recording along with a great live performance inside.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Roll of the Dice: We’ve Got to Do It Now
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: "We've Got to Do It Now" is a Steel Mill-era anti-war song with co-lead vocals by Bruce and Robbin Thompson.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Roll of the Dice: I Gotta Be Free
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Short on lyrics, long on guitar jams, "I Gotta Be Free" is an early Springsteen original from his Steel Mill period with a mid-song cover of The Grateful Dead's "Turn on Your Love Light."
